definition: A criterion is a standard that something must meet in order to be judged, chosen, or approved.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word criterion. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know criterion should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Price was never the panel's criterion; every bid was judged on its safety record alone.
A guideline is softer than a criterion: guidelines advise and can bend for a good reason, while a criterion is a standard that must actually be met before something passes.

Prerequisite is more binding than criterion — a criterion is one standard among several in the judging, but a prerequisite is the locked door before judging even begins: fail it and you are never considered at all.

A benchmark is usually a number — a fixed reference point that performance is measured against, like last quarter's sales. A criterion can be any quality or condition that must be met, no arithmetic required.
Yardstick is the informal cousin: a rough measure you hold things against for comparison. A criterion is more official — a stated standard with pass and fail on either side of it.

A criterion is a standard that something must meet in order to be judged, chosen, or approved.
Abara let the class pick the criterion for the paper-airplane title before a single plane flew: distance, airtime, or surviving three throws intact.
They argued for a full period and chose airtime.
From that moment the winner was decided in principle — the slow, wide gliders would beat the sleek darts every time — and the dart builders knew it the instant the vote closed.
Criterion is the exact word because the class wasn't choosing a winner; it was choosing the standard that would choose the winner.
That's the power the word names: set the test and you've half-decided the results.
One more thing worth keeping: criterion is the singular — one standard is a criterion, several are criteria, and careful writers never let "a criteria" slip past.
Criterion is the word for a stated, defensible standard — and it is strictly singular: one criterion, several criteria, and "a criteria" marks a writer faster than any misspelling.
This unit's judicious describes the person doing the weighing well; a criterion is what the weighing rests on.
Where the standard is just a number to beat, benchmark is the honest word.

The children's book award nearly fell apart in its second year.
Each judge championed a different favorite, and the arguments circled for weeks without landing.
The fix was a single published criterion: to win, a book had to be one that a nine-year-old could finish alone and want to read again.
Suddenly the arguing had somewhere to stand.
Gorgeous books that bored their readers fell away, and the committee's shortlist, once a mirror of the judges' tastes, began to look like the library's most-renewed list instead.
